target_customer: Brazilian companies of all sizes, notably those with heavy ad spend and fuel or travel spending, that want virtual cards and expense control
problem: Companies in Brazil struggle to pay suppliers and platforms and to control spending by team or project. Portao 3 issues virtual cards and tracks expenses, described as Ramp for LATAM.
business_model: Fintech take on card spend and expense management software, reaching profitability per press

founders.name: Fernando Nery
founders.role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, sole CEO from April 2024
prior_employers: Zup (CPO for 5 years, per YC page)
previous_startups: A prior company with a successful exit, name not given on the YC page
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, described as second-time entrepreneur. Education not found.

founders.name: Bianca Junqueira
previous_startups: Funded startups in travel and growth (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Surname appears as Pereira in some sources and Junqueira in others. Left the co-CEO role to focus on personal projects per press (2024).

technical_complexity.rationale: Issuing virtual cards and reconciling spend requires payment and card-issuer integrations and compliance, standard for fintech but heavier than plain software.

defensibility.rationale: Spend data and workflows create some stickiness, but card issuing sits on third-party rails and Brazilian rivals offered similar products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. A 2023 article lists VExpenses, Jeeves, Conta Simples, Onfly and Payfy as players in corporate spend management.

market_need_then: The company started as corporate travel software and moved toward cards after finding demand for payment control, and bootstrapped to profitability before its seed according to press. No quantified market data was gathered.

identity.voice_and_tone: Efficiency and autonomy, with claims like 3x more efficiency

brand_strength.rationale: Local fintech press coverage of its funding and hires but nothing on the brand itself, and the Portuguese name with a cedilla and tilde is hard for non-Portuguese speakers.

pivots.why: Press describes a move from travel software to a cards and spend platform that reached profitability, per Seedtable and Startups.com.br.

outcome_analysis: Portao 3 bootstrapped, joined YC in S21 and raised a R$19M (about US$3.6M) seed in January 2023 led by Better Tomorrow Ventures after pivoting from corporate travel to cards. It claims thousands of client companies. Co-CEO Bianca left in 2024 leaving Fernando Nery as sole CEO. No exit or shutdown found.
notes: Seed of R$19M (about US$3.6M per Seedtable and LatamFintech) is reported by Forbes Brasil, Startups.com.br and Panrotas; the USD figure is a press conversion. The YC $125K standard deal is not a round. No competitor with a source dated near mid 2021 was found; the 2023 article lists VExpenses, Jeeves, Conta Simples, Onfly and Payfy but that is after the batch, so they are not listed. Founder education not found. The company site claims thousands of clients and R$6B transacted with inconsistent figures, unverified.
